points.description: Gives the final answer 510510 (= 2·3·5·7·11·13·17) and reaches it by a fully valid argument. The argument must show: (a) the gcd divides P(1)=17!, so only primes ≤17 can divide it; (b) for each prime p ≤ 17 and every n, p divides P(n) (if p∤n, pick k in 1..p-1 with kn+1≡0 mod p; for p=2 use n+1 for odd n); (c) each such prime appears only to the first power, e.g. via n=p, where n·(n+1)·(kn+1) has p-adic valuation exactly 1 (or an equivalent check). Any invalid step, missing key justification, or a wrong final answer earns 0.

rubric.notes: Full mark only if the reasoning is valid throughout (primes bounded by 17 via P(1), each prime ≤17 divides every P(n), exponent exactly 1 shown) and the answer is 510510. Any wrong step or wrong final answer earns 0. There are no part marks.
rubric.answer_key: P(1)=1·2·3·…·17=17!, so any common divisor has only primes ≤17. For prime p≤17 and any n: if p|n, p|P(n). Otherwise n is invertible mod p, so choose k in {1,…,p−1}⊆{1,…,16} with kn≡−1 (mod p); then p | kn+1, a factor of P(n) (for p=2, n odd gives n+1 even). So every prime ≤17 divides all P(n). Exponents: take n=p; P(p)=p·(p+1)·(2p+1)…(16p+1), and every factor except the first is ≡1 mod p, so v_p(P(p))=1. So each prime appears exactly to the first power. gcd = 2·3·5·7·11·13·17 = 510510.
